angles: Agent observability vs. LLM observability: the differentiator is tool-call and task-level tracing, not just latency/token metrics — a live dashboard must show the reasoning path, tool invocations, and retries

The 'silent failure' problem: agentic AI degrades quietly (hallucination, wrong tool, drift) without triggering traditional alerts, so real-time dashboards need quality/behavior signals, not just uptime
OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions as the emerging interoperability standard — vendor-neutral telemetry that outlives tooling choices
Buyer tradeoff in 2026: dedicated AI tools (LangSmith, Langfuse, Arize) vs. APM-native platforms (Datadog, New Relic) — correlation with infra vs. deep eval/review/feedback loops
Data sovereignty and cost governance: self-hosted options (Langfuse, Langtrace, OpenObserve) and token-spend monitoring matter more as agents scale and token budgets blow out
Market churn/consolidation: Langfuse acquired by ClickHouse, acquisitions in the space mean today's independent tool may be a platform module tomorrow
Pricing as a deciding factor: agent traces generate thousands of spans (high-cardinality) so metered/span-based pricing can dominate TCO
